title: Apple-Pecan Butter Smoked Chicken Thighs
summary: Mildly seasoned chicken thighs smoked low, finished hot, and brushed with a sweet-savory apple-pecan BBQ glaze.
sourceNote: An apple-pecan butter pantry find inspires a smoke-forward chicken dinner with a familiar, mild BBQ glaze. Proposed recipe; awaiting its first cooking verdict.

ingredients.note: optional; omit for a mild version
plus 1–2 tsp if needed to balance a very sweet apple butter
1–2 tbsp as needed to make the glaze brushable

steps.text: Pat 6–8 bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs dry and lightly coat with 1 tbsp neutral oil. Combine 1½ tsp kosher salt, 1½ tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp onion powder, ¾ tsp black pepper, 1 tsp brown sugar, and ½ tsp dried thyme. Omit cayenne for mild chicken, or add up to ¼ tsp. Season all over and under the skin where accessible. Optionally refrigerate uncovered for a few hours to dry the skin.

Mix ⅓ cup apple-pecan butter, ¼ cup mild BBQ sauce, 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar, 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, 1 tbsp Dijon mustard, 1 tsp soy sauce, and ½ tsp garlic powder. Thin with 1–2 tbsp water. Taste for apple-forward, sweet-savory balance; add 1–2 tsp more vinegar if overly sweet. Before any brush touches the chicken, reserve ¼ cup in a separate clean container for serving.
Preheat the pellet smoker to 225°F. Pecan, apple, cherry, or a mild hickory pellet works well. Use a grate-level thermometer if the controller temperature is unreliable.

Place the thighs skin-side up and smoke without glaze for approximately 60–75 minutes, checking at 60 minutes. Aim for roughly 140–150°F in the thickest part, away from bone. This is an intermediate temperature, not the finished safe temperature; proceed directly to the hot finish.

Raise the smoker to 375°F and continue cooking for approximately 15–20 minutes before glazing. Timing depends on thigh size and how quickly the smoker heats; check internal temperature and skin as you go.
Brush on a thin layer of the cooking glaze. Cook at 375°F for about 10 minutes, watching for scorching, then apply a second thin layer.

Continue cooking until the thickest part of each thigh reaches about 180–185°F, checking away from bone. Poultry must reach at least 165°F; the higher target gives thighs a more tender texture. If the skin needs more browning and the glaze is not dark, optionally finish at 400–425°F for 5–8 minutes, watching continuously because the sugars can burn. Do not chase crisp skin at the expense of scorching the glaze.

Rest the chicken for 5–10 minutes. Warm the clean, reserved ¼ cup glaze separately and spoon a little over the cooked thighs using a clean utensil. Discard leftover glaze used with the cooking brush. Serve with mac and cheese and green beans if desired.
